scope: 12 concepts novos, bebê/criança/jovem das quatro famílias; adultos preservados. Novos nomes e relações propostos.

families.name: Alvorraia
families.story: Primeiro flutua à deriva, depois aprende a colher corrente nas velas, manobrar e finalmente erguer outros sobre obstáculos.
forms: EARLIEST tiny ray-kite: one compact soft ivory diamond-shaped folded head-body, gentle violet eyes integrated into front fold, two TINY coral/turquoise lateral corner flaps only, no distinct head/neck or adult scroll lobes. One bamboo top bow, mint knot at bottom and ONE short braided rabiola ending a small coral fan. Three/four big smooth planes, simple cute manga, no armor or intricate patterns. Slight floating tilt, broad calm face with little curved folded mouth, not a baby bird.

SMALL juvenile living paper ray, short rounded ivory central body and TWO independent wide cupped turquoise/coral sail fins with navy undersides, violet curious eyes on broad little ray face, two small uncurled cephalic flap buds. One thin bamboo leading support per fin, two mint knots, ONE short braided rabiola and simple fan terminal. No legs, no armor, no adult chest keel or giant curled scroll lobes. Learning to gather flow: one fin cups upward, other balances. New body separate from wings but compact, only few graphic current marks.

ADOLESCENT agile narrow central paper-ray body, TWO long slim swept sail fins, ivory/coral/turquoise with navy underplanes, youthful angular ray face and violet eyes, two HALF-curled cephalic guide lobes not the complete large adult scrolls. Sparse copper leading-corner guards ONLY, bamboo leading ribs and mint knot anchors, small smooth keel with one modest braided tide knot. No legs, no crystal, no adult enormous mantle/mass. One complete slender rabiola with coral fan. Banking dynamically into a curve, tips swept back, sail silhouette thinner than adult, broad clean paper planes.

families.name: Coroabissal
families.story: Aprende a manter o próprio volume, sustentar a pressão de uma pequena corrente e repartir a carga pelo dorso antes de proteger uma passagem inteira.
forms: EARLIEST very simple small living paper whale float, rounded navy head-body integrated, one ivory folded lower smile-plane, gentle mint eyes, TWO tiny lateral flipper tabs, tiny short paired horizontal caudal fold behind. ONE small rolled WINE paper flap on back hints pressure chamber, not an elaborate shell. One little red knot and thin short soul-rabiola with tiny ivory shell terminal distinct from caudal fold. Just three/four big masses, no mature armor or teeth. Calm buoyant little creature, no normal plush whale realism.

SMALL curious juvenile living-paper whale, short cobalt/navy body with ivory belly, WINE red broad side plane, TWO developed short flippers and TWO little horizontal tail lobes, gentle mint eyes and folded whale jaw. Back has one open HALF-CURL paper flap supported by a simple bamboo rib, not adult big full spiral. One red knot below jaw, ONE separate thin braided rabiola rooted at upper tail base ending a tiny shell flag. No legs, no crown or adult flipper armor, no teeth. Body has broad tensioned paper folds, playful turn showing buoyancy control.

ADOLESCENT sleek athletic living paper whale, longer narrower navy/wine body than massive adult, ivory lower jaw and belly, smaller focused mint eyes under short folded brow. TWO long slender flippers, TWO horizontal tail lobes. Growing dorsal chamber is a PARTIAL OPEN C-shaped paper spiral with only two big ribs and red anchors, not full adult circular nautilus shell. Light copper forehead rim and shoulder-fin guard only. ONE fine braided rabiola at upper rear root with shell terminal, no legs or crystal. Forward pushing swimming stance, broad paper pressure volumes, slim body contrasting adult depth and huge crown.

families.name: Vortentáculo
families.story: Do novelo que agarra sem distinguir ao coordenador que aprende a soltar um ponto para liberar o próximo; o controle amadurece antes da força.
forms: EARLIEST simple little living-paper octopus seed: one squat PLUM teardrop mantle with gentle ice-blue eyes integrated near lower edge and ONE ivory forehead crease. EIGHT very short rounded folded arm-tassels at bottom, all attached around same base; four in front and four behind with separate tips, no long twisting arms. Broad OCHRE underside on a few visible tabs. No adult triple crown, cuffs, siphon or armor. ONE thin purple/ivory braided rabiola from back top with tiny crescent terminal, clearly distinct from tiny arm tassels. Few large smooth paper surfaces, simple clean cute manga.

SMALL juvenile living paper octopus, squat violet rounded mantle with TWO small broad folded crest tabs only, curious ice-blue eyes. EXACTLY EIGHT short flexible arms with separate tips: four front spreading broad, four rear slightly raised. OCHRE undersides, only one or two large braided knot suction-discs on some arms, no armored cuffs. Small side folded siphon starts developing, smooth broad paper curves, one simple bamboo mantle arc. ONE thin soul-rabiola attached upper back with little crescent flag. Playful testing grips, no props, no adult tall three-plate crown or massive arms.

ADOLESCENT alert living paper octopus, narrow upright PLUM/VIOLET mantle and TWO folded upper crown vanes only (adult has three massive stacked waves). Focused ice-blue eyes, small short folded siphon. EXACTLY EIGHT arms: four long foreground arms in distinct S curves and four smaller rear arms raised, each rooted and with one tip. OCHRE/ivory underside, a few large knot suction-discs, bamboo segments at bases. Light copper cuff ONLY on TWO leading arms, remaining six unarmored, no huge adult four gauntlets. ONE very thin braided soul-rabiola rooted high back with purple crescent terminal. Coordinated reaching gesture, lighter agile proportions, no human hands/legs or crystal.

families.name: Reciférreo
families.story: Aprende a apoiar o próprio abrigo, ancorar um lado e proteger o outro, até reconhecer o momento de soltar a proteção para permitir o retorno da água.
forms: EARLIEST tiny living-paper crustacean pebble packet, compact single flat CELADON folded head-body shell, two short icy-PINK eye-stalk nubs with friendly eyes, ivory little folded mouth. TWO tiny tucked walking-foot tabs and TWO very small pincer buds at front, no developed walking legs or armor. One saffron bamboo edge, one little simple knot and ONE short braided rabiola ending a small stepped tidal-notch flag. One shell plane only, no adult terraces or dorsal kelp sails. Very simple few clear shapes, cute but manga not rendered plush.

SMALL juvenile paper crustacean, exactly SIX SHORT walking legs (THREE per side) plus TWO small front pincer arms. ONE broad flat celadon shell plate with charcoal underside and saffron trim, two short eye stalks with curious icy pink eyes, ivory jaw fold. Pincers modest: one flatter spoon-like, one small hook, no adult huge shield. ONE little partly folded dorsal kelp vane only, one thin bamboo perimeter rib and few saffron knots. ONE short braided rabiola stepped flag. No heavy leg armor, no three-tier adult fortress; all six supporting feet spaced so no seventh foot.

ADOLESCENT mobile paper crustacean, exactly SIX walking legs (THREE each side) plus TWO front pincer arms, no other limbs. Body lower and narrower than adult but legs LONGER, raised alert stance. TWO offset celadon/charcoal shell terraces (adult has three huge ones), TWO small partly opened folded kelp vanes behind; saffron bamboo edges and functional knots. Icy pink focused eye stalks, small ivory mandibles, light charcoal guards on only front leg roots. One medium fan-shaped pincer-shield and one medium anchoring hook claw; adult claws much broader. ONE complete braided soul-rabiola with stepped flag. Readable six feet and two claw roots, clean broad paper folds, no crystal or realistic crab texture.
